Definition: from G1909 and G2480; to avail further, i.e. (figuratively) insist stoutly:--be the more fierce.
BiblicalUsage: Epischyo means to grow stronger, to insist more fiercely — and the chief priests were the more fierce, saying, He stirreth up the people, teaching throughout all Jewry, beginning from Galilee to this place.
TheologicalSignificance: Louder, not truer: that is what accusation becomes when it has no case, and Pilate heard the volume, not the evidence.
